problems.title: An average reveals the number of boys
problems.question: 24 pupils average 8 points. Girls average 6 and boys 9. How many boys are there?
problems.idea: Use a weighted total.

problems.title: Sum the two roots of an absolute-value equation
problems.question: Find the sum of the roots of |−6q−1|=2.
problems.idea: Split into the two sign possibilities.
steps: The roots are q=−1/2 and q=1/6.
Their sum is −3/6+1/6.

problems.title: A short angle chase gives a perimeter
problems.question: In isosceles ABC, AB=BC=4.8 dm and B=36°. Bisectors AM,CN meet at T. Find perimeter CMT.
problems.idea: Use the equal angles to identify equal segments.
steps: In ABM, angles A and B are 36°, so AM=BM.
In ACT, both base angles are 36°, so AT=CT.
In CMT, angle C is 36° and the other two angles are 72°, so CT=CM.
Thus MT=AM−AT=BM−CM, and perimeter CMT=2CM+MT=BM+CM=BC.

problems.title: Signs repeat in a multiplicative recurrence
problems.question: A sequence starts −1,2; each later term is the product of the preceding two. Among its first 100 terms, how many are negative?
problems.idea: Only the signs matter.
steps: Every block of three has two negative terms.
The first 99 terms contain 33·2=66 negatives. The 100th starts the next block and is negative.

problems.title: Inverse-proportional parts with an incorrect choice list
problems.question: Split 0.66 into parts inversely proportional to 5/2,5/3,5/6. Find the greatest part.
problems.idea: Invert the ratio numbers.
steps: There are 11 units; the largest part is 6 units.
problems.note: None of the printed choices equals 0.36.

problems.title: Recover triangle angles from exterior-angle sums
problems.question: In the printed triangle, exterior angles satisfy x+y=234° and z+x=246°. Find A:B:C.
problems.idea: The three adjacent exterior angles total 360°.
steps: In the diagram z is at A, x at B, y at C. Hence A=54°,B=60°,C=66°.
Divide by 6.

problems.title: A proportion with mixed numbers
problems.question: Solve x:2⅔=6¾:1.8.
problems.idea: Convert to fractions.
steps: The right ratio is (27/4)/(9/5)=15/4.

problems.title: A sum of distances on a number line
problems.question: Find the minimum of |x+2.3|+|x+3.2|.
problems.idea: It is the sum of distances to −2.3 and −3.2.
steps: The two fixed points are 0.9 apart.
Equality occurs for every x between −3.2 and −2.3.

problems.title: Simplify a nested arithmetic expression
problems.question: Evaluate (0.5:1.5−3⅓·0.6):(1−3½).
problems.idea: Convert the divisions and mixed numbers to exact fractions.
steps: The first bracket is −5/3, and the second is −5/2.
Their quotient is (−5/3)/(−5/2)=2/3.

problems.title: Erase a digit to divide a number by sixteen
problems.question: Find the sum of all four-digit numbers that become sixteen times smaller after the first digit is erased.
problems.idea: Separate the first digit from the last three.
steps: 15b=1000a gives b=200a/3, so a must be 3,6,9.
The original numbers are 3200,6400,9600.
Their sum is 19200.

problems.title: Exactly one solution of an absolute-value equation
problems.question: For which a does a|x|=a+1 have exactly one real solution?
problems.idea: |x|=t has one solution only at t=0.
steps: The right side must be zero, giving a=−1.
At a=0 the equation is 0=1 and has no solution. Positive right sides give two roots, negative ones none.

problems.title: Equal work in worker-hours
problems.question: Four masons build a wall in 8 days at 9 hours per day. How many days for six masons at 6 hours per day?
problems.idea: The total worker-hours is fixed.

problems.title: Pay for food actually given to guests
problems.question: Three shepherds contribute 5,6,9 cakes to a meal shared equally by them and two tourists. The tourists pay 20 lari each. How much should the third shepherd receive?
problems.idea: Subtract each shepherd’s own share before allocating the payment.
formulas: 20 cakes shared by 5 people gives 4 each.
steps: The shepherds give the tourists 1,2,5 cakes respectively, a total of 8.
The third supplied 5/8 of the guests’ food and receives 5/8 of 40 lari.
problems.note: The wording mistakenly calls the cake contributors tourists; the three contributors must be the shepherds for the described sharing problem.

problems.title: Specify which sides make each triangle isosceles
problems.question: In isosceles ABC with B=40°, K,M lie on ray AC and triangles ABK,CBM are isosceles. Find angle KBM.
problems.idea: Under the intended equalities AK=AB and CM=CB, chase the base angles.
steps: K lies beyond C, so angle CBK=55°−40°=15°.
In BCM, the angle at C is 110°; the equal sides CB=CM give angle CBM=35°.
Thus angle KBM=35°−15°=20°.
problems.answer: Intended answer 20°; it appears twice in the choices.
problems.note: The isosceles equalities are not specified. Another allowed choice BK=AK with CM=CB gives angle KBM=5°. The 20° answer assumes the intended side equalities above.

problems.title: A noninteger truck requirement must be rounded up
problems.question: One truck moves 50 tonnes over 30 km in 6 hours. How many identical trucks are needed to move 40 tonnes over 60 km in 4 hours?
problems.idea: Compare the tonne-kilometres per available hour.
steps: Two trucks cannot do the required work.
The least whole number at least 2.4 is 3.

problems.title: Two nested midpoints on a number line
problems.question: K is midpoint of M,D and N is midpoint of K,D. Find (k−d)/(n−m).
problems.idea: Write their midpoint coordinates.
steps: k−d=(m−d)/2, while n−m=3(d−m)/4.
Their quotient is −2/3. Distinct endpoints ensure the denominator is nonzero.

problems.title: Four outer angles around an equilateral triangle
problems.question: AK,CM,BD meet at a point, with MNK equilateral in the printed configuration. Find A+B+C+D.
problems.idea: Use the angle sums in the two outer triangles.
formulas: The two angles at the common point have sum 180°−60°=120°.
steps: The other angles of the two triangles total 2·180°−120°.
Those other angles are precisely A,B,C,D.

problems.title: Combine two side ratios
problems.question: AB:BC=2:3 and BC:AC=4:5. The perimeter is 14 cm. Find the largest side.
problems.idea: Make the common BC ratio match.
steps: The ratio sum is 35, so one unit is 14/35=0.4 cm.
The largest side is AC=15·0.4.

problems.title: An equation whose variable cancels
problems.question: Solve 3−(2x−1)/2=2−(3x−1)/3.
problems.idea: Simplify both sides before trying to isolate x.
steps: Adding x to both sides leaves 7/2=7/3, a false statement.
No x can satisfy it.
problems.note: The printed choices are ordinary numbers and do not include the empty solution set.

problems.title: Count integer-sided isosceles triangles
problems.question: How many isosceles triangles have positive integer sides and perimeter 20?
problems.idea: Write the equal sides as a and the base as 20−2a.
steps: These give 5<a<10.
The integer values a=6,7,8,9 give four valid, distinct triangles.

problems.title: Two arrival times determine a distance
problems.question: A cyclist arrives 10 minutes before a bus leaves at 15 km/h, but would arrive 5 minutes after at 12 km/h. Find the distance.
problems.idea: The difference in travel times is 15 minutes.
steps: The left side is d/60, so d/60=1/4.

problems.title: Balance silver in two alloys
problems.question: The silver:gold ratios are 2:3 and 4:1. Mix p grams of the first with q grams of the second to obtain equal masses of silver and gold. Find p:q.
problems.idea: The final silver fraction is 1/2.
steps: Multiply by 10: 4p+8q=5p+5q.
Thus p=3q.

problems.title: A perimeter from an altitude and a bisector
problems.question: In isosceles MNK, MK=KN=a, MN=b and a+b=24. Altitude NR and bisector KS meet at O; KO=2SN. Find perimeter ORK.
problems.idea: The bisector from K also bisects MN, so KO=b. Use right triangles and the angle-bisector theorem.
formulas: Put KR=x, OR=y. KO²=x²+y²=b²; MR=a−x; NR²=a²−x².
steps: The angle-bisector theorem in triangle KNR gives NO/OR=a/x, so NR=y(a+x)/x. Squaring and using NR²=a²−x² gives y²=x²(a−x)/(a+x).
Also MN²=MR²+NR²=(a−x)²+a²−x²=2a(a−x)=b².
Combine b²=x²+y²=2ax²/(a+x) with b²=2a(a−x). Thus 2x²=a².
Substituting back gives y²=(a−x)², so y=a−x.
The required perimeter is KO+KR+OR=b+x+(a−x)=a+b.

problems.title: A perpendicular bisector replaces a side length
problems.question: In isosceles ABC with base AC, the perpendicular bisector of AB meets AC at D. Leg:base=3:5 and perimeter=6.6 cm. Find perimeter BDC.
problems.idea: D is equally distant from A and B.
steps: Let each leg be 3t and base 5t. Then 11t=6.6, so t=0.6.

problems.title: A correct angle absent from the choices
problems.question: BD is a median in triangle ABC with BD=AC/2. Find A if A=4C.
problems.idea: A hypotenuse-length median identifies a right triangle.
formulas: DA=DB=DC, so the circle with centre D contains A,B,C and AC is a diameter; B=90°.
steps: Thus A+C=90°. With A=4C, 5C=90° gives C=18° and A=72°.
problems.note: The source says A is four times C. The listed 18° is C, not A; 72° is missing from the choices.
